primary_diagnosis_treated: End-Stage Renal Disease due to Diabetic Nephropathy
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) and NICE NG107 (Renal replacement therapy and conservative management)

medications.purpose: Renal protection and blood pressure control in CKD with proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension and to monitor creatinine and potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually; consider switch to loop diuretic if eGFR <30 and inadequate response
medications.nice_justification: NG203 lists thiazide as adjunct BP control; note reduced efficacy when eGFR <30

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and lipid profile in 4‑12 weeks
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a risk‑equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 5 mg once daily, titrate to 10 mg over 4‑6 weeks if needed
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after titration
medications.purpose: Achieve BP target <130/80 mmHg in proteinuric CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 BP target <130/80 mmHg for proteinuric CKD; amlodipine is recommended as add‑on therapy

medications.dose: 800 mg three times daily with meals
medications.duration: Until serum phosphate <1.5 mmol/L, then review every 3 months
medications.nice_justification: NG107 lists sevelamer as first‑line phosphate binder for CKD stage 5

medications.duration: Until corrected calcium 2.1‑2.6 mmol/L and PTH within target, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Treat secondary hyperparathyroidism / vitamin D deficiency
medications.nice_justification: NG107 recommends vitamin D analogues for secondary hyperparathyroidism in CKD

medications.dose: 500 mg single dose (repeat based on ferritin/TSAT)
medications.duration: Single dose; repeat as needed after iron studies
medications.purpose: Replete iron stores before ESA therapy
medications.nice_justification: NG107 recommends IV iron for iron deficiency (ferritin <200 µg/L or TSAT <20%) in CKD

medications.dose: 5,000 IU weekly (dose titrated to Hb 100‑120 g/L)
medications.duration: Until hemoglobin target achieved, then review every 3 months
medications.nice_justification: NG107 recommends ESA for CKD anemia when Hb <100 g/L after iron repletion

medications.duration: Until serum bicarbonate >20 mmol/L, then review every 3 months
medications.nice_justification: NG107 recommends sodium bicarbonate for CKD patients with bicarbonate <20 mmol/L

medications.duration: Ongoing — review at each clinic visit
medications.nice_justification: Standard diabetes management; essential for patients with ESRD to avoid hypoglycaemia

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood pressure lowering; risk of symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Start amlodipine at 5 mg, monitor BP and symptoms after 1 week; adjust dose if needed

interactions_checked.interaction: Synergistic antihypertensive effect; may increase potassium retention
interactions_checked.action: Monitor serum potassium and renal function in 1‑2 weeks after any dose change

interactions_checked.interaction: ESA can raise blood pressure; ACE‑I may blunt this effect but still requires monitoring
interactions_checked.action: Check BP weekly after ESA initiation and adjust antihypertensives as needed

interactions_checked.interaction: Sevelamer can bind statins and reduce absorption
interactions_checked.action: Take atorvastatin with the evening meal and sevelamer with main meals; separate by at least 1 hour

interactions_checked.interaction: Increased sodium load may attenuate antihypertensive effect
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure and fluid status; adjust lisinopril dose if needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR 9 mL/min/1.73 m² (<30) – high risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: Discontinue metformin; optimise glycaemic control with insulin

contraindications.reason: CKD stage 5 – accelerate renal decline and cause fluid retention
contraindications.alternative: Use paracetamol for pain; avoid NSAIDs

contraindications.reason: Patient already on ACE‑I; dual RAAS blockade is contraindicated (NG203)
contraindications.alternative: Continue ACE‑I alone; do not add ARB

contraindications.reason: Risk of hyperkalaemia in advanced CKD
contraindications.alternative: Avoid potassium supplements; monitor serum K⁺

contraindications.reason: eGFR 9 mL/min/1.73 m² is below the recommended 20‑45 mL/min range (TA775)
contraindications.alternative: Not indicated at this renal function

assumptions_warnings: Serum potassium, calcium, phosphate, PTH, bicarbonate, hemoglobin, ferritin, TSAT, lipid profile and liver function tests are not available – these must be obtained before initiating ESA, iron, statin, vitamin D analogue and sodium bicarbonate.
A1c reported as 2.9 % is likely erroneous; repeat HbA1c to guide insulin dosing.
Allergy status not documented – verify no allergy to statins, ACE‑I, iron preparations, or vitamin D analogues before prescribing.
Weight/BMI not provided for weight‑based dosing of ESA; standard adult dosing used pending weight confirmation.
Blood pressure target assumes proteinuria (ACR ≥30 mg/mmol); confirm ACR to apply <130/80 mmHg target.
treatment_summary: The plan continues ACE‑I and thiazide therapy, adds a high‑intensity statin, and introduces amlodipine to achieve BP <130/80 mmHg. Renal‑specific treatments for ESRD are initiated: sevelamer for phosphate control, alfacalcidol for secondary hyperparathyroidism, IV iron followed by epoetin alfa for anemia, and sodium bicarbonate for metabolic acidosis. All additions follow NICE NG203/NG107 recommendations, avoid contraindicated drugs, and include monitoring of electrolytes, renal function, hemoglobin, lipid profile, calcium‑phosphate balance, and blood pressure. Assumptions and missing labs are flagged for urgent review.
